title: [finding] cli checklist: build-own-contract clause 4 vs flag-command-error-ux disagree on exit code 2 — narrow clause 4 to the #4873 duration-leak
body:
## Symptom
Two items in the `cli` checklist area disagree about exit code 2. `cli.build-own-contract` clause 4 (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json:145` — "exit codes are exactly 0 or 1 (the CliExitCode union) — never a count, never a duration") treats a config-load-time throw that exits **2** as a violation, while `cli.flag-command-error-ux` asserts that exit **2** IS the correct oclif `ExitError` code. In the run, a config-load-time throw on the human path exits 2 (reproduced twice) because `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts`'s catch ends in `this.error()` and oclif's `ExitError` is 2; the `CliExitCode 0|1` type only narrows the `emitJson`/`emitText` slot. Every `--json` invocation exits cleanly (0/1/1/1).

## Root cause
Checklist reconciliation, not a product defect. Clause 4 was written to pin the #4873 duration-in-exit-slot leak (a timer value reaching the exit-code slot), not to forbid oclif's standard error exit. As phrased it collides with `flag-command-error-ux`, which correctly treats exit 2 as the oclif error exit. The clause should be narrowed to the #4873 duration-leak it exists to catch, so a legitimate oclif `ExitError` (2) on a config-load-time throw no longer reads as a violation.

## Reproduction
Run a `build`/`compile` invocation whose config fails to load at load time on the human (non-`--json`) path; observe exit 2 from `compile.ts`'s `this.error()` catch. Compare against `cli.flag-command-error-ux`, which asserts exit 2 as the correct oclif `ExitError`. The two checklist clauses cannot both hold as written. On `origin/main` the clause text (`cli.json:145`) and `compile.ts`'s `this.error()` catch (lines 411, 480) are unchanged, so the reconciliation is still needed.

## Source
Extracted from the QA run objectstack-ai/objectstack#7628 (framework 92f26f75, console 6314e87f).
